    Tonight Engine v8

    Four AI analysts grade every leg blind, with no market price shown, and our grade is the middle of their numbers plus our own system grade. Kalshi referees after that. When our grade is 8 or more above Kalshi, the leg is removed from the board, the Hammer and every ticket, and listed here as market disagrees. It is still graded the next morning, so we can see whether the market or the models were right.

    EXPERIMENTAL · beta · be cautious

    Latest perfect parlay attempt

    An experiment that learns. Every night the model re-reads every graded leg we have, works out which kinds of legs have hit more or less often than our grade suggests (stat, safer vs regular line, grade band, sport, over or under), and posts the clues it found. Then it scores tonight's legs with what it learned and builds its best Perfect 3 and Perfect 10x attempts before the games. Each attempt is saved and graded the next morning, and that result becomes part of what it learns from. It is not proven, and a hot streak would not prove it either.

    EXPERIMENTAL · hindsight lab

    The perfect parlay

    Hindsight only, never offered: for every past night, the parlay we could have built using only picks that hit. One 3-5x and one 10x+. Payouts are estimated from our grades, not real Kalshi prices. Nobody can bet hindsight. The point is to study what the winning legs had in common.

    What perfect parlays are made of

    BETA · EXPERIMENTAL · not a recommendation

    Beta Test Mode

    A test of one question: can our model find player lines priced around even money (+100 to -150) that hit more often than the price says? This is separate from the main picks and the Hammer. A simulation is an estimate, not proof a line will hit. Nothing here has beaten the market on new picks yet.

    Tonight's agent simulations

    From Nov 21 the simulations come from our own Python model only (below, run at 1:17 PM PT with fresh prices and injuries). It beat the market on Nov 20 and costs nothing to run. The four AI agents keep grading every leg blind on the main board, where we are scoring their accuracy.

    Track record so far

    graded the next morning

    Our own sim · Top list

    Independent check, Nov 19 (experimental): ChatGPT ran its own simulation from its own game logs (40,000 draws per line). 5 of its top 8 lines were also in our top 8, with similar hit rates (Wagler 84% vs our 81%, Garland 81% vs 83%). That checks the math. It does not show an edge, because both use the same kind of data. Gemini and Grok did not simulate.

    Which methods actually find value?

    tested on picks not used to build them

    History: 603 graded legs with an exact Kalshi price, Nov 4 to 17. Each method was built on Nov 4 to 12 (300 legs) and then checked on Nov 13 to 17 (303 legs). ROI means buying at Kalshi's price including its fee. Many legs share a game or a player ladder, so the true uncertainty is wider than the ranges shown.

    8-leg ticket

    status

    Not ready. An 8-leg ticket only makes sense once a method has beaten break-even on new picks over a large sample, and once same-game correlation is priced in. We will not force one for the payout. Every Top 15 line is saved with its price, the price time and the simulated hit rate, and graded the next day, so this page builds its own track record.

    The finding that matters

    Our "edges" are where we lose
    8 of 20

    On props where our grade was 8 or more points above Kalshi's price, the leg hit 8 of 20. On props graded 70+ where Kalshi was at or above our grade, the leg hit 28 of 32 (88%). Two nights in a row, the market was closer than we were every time we disagreed with it.

    A big gap is a warning sign
    The Power 3 was built on those edges
    0 of 3

    Carter 6+ rebounds (we said 88, Kalshi 78) had 3. Jokic 8+ assists (87 vs 74) had 7. Zion 20+ (75 vs 64) had 16. We picked them because we liked them more than the market did. That is the mistake.

    Build from here

    Going forward

    1. Our grades stay our grades

    We keep grading every line the same way: season record, last five games, injuries, matchup. That is what built the record.

    2. Kalshi's price sits next to every grade

    The board, the Top 25 and the app's Picks list now show Kalshi's price beside our grade, so you can see the odds when you build a parlay.

    3. Only the cappers' picks

    We can move a line up or down in the same stat. We do not add new stats or players to the board.

    4. You build the parlays

    Pick your favorites off the grades. When our grade and Kalshi are far apart, that is a leg to look at twice.

    Model v7, starting Monday

    1. NFL props capped at 75

    Until we have 100 graded NFL legs, no NFL yardage or catch leg is graded above 75, whatever the season record says.

    2. Matchup on every leg

    Each pick shows what the opponent allows at that stat and where that ranks. A bad matchup docks the grade. No bad matchup goes on a main ticket.

    3. Kalshi's price is a second opinion

    We log Kalshi's price next to our grade. When Kalshi is 15 or more below us, our grade moves halfway to it.

    4. One leg, two tickets

    The same leg, not just the same player, goes on two tickets at most.

    Model v6 · four changes

    1. Small samples get pulled toward Kalshi's price. "12 of 12" this season becomes about 85, not 93. Rookies with under 15 games cap at 80.
    2. The blowout rule covers both teams. Any game with a spread of 10+: no props from either side on main tickets.
    3. One player, two tickets, hard stop. Friends' tickets count too.
    4. Play small and set a nightly limit before the first game. The Power 3 gets the biggest share, everything else less. No college spreads unless we have the team's numbers.

    Model v5 · three changes

    1. Blowout rule. When a favorite is 65%+ to win, no underdog spreads in that game and no bench-risk props (bigs' rebounds) on the favorite. One blowout can't sink more than one ticket.
    2. The 3-leg is the daily core. Three legs from the 70 pool, moneyline favorites first, priced 65-80% on Kalshi. It's 2 for 2 the last two nights and hits about 61% at our record.
    3. No 100x lottos. 0 for 22. Fun tickets stay small, 2-3% of the night.

                                                    Build from the list first, every day

                                                    Why an extra 90% leg can shrink your payout

                                                    Think of Kalshi like a toll road. Every leg you add, Kalshi takes a small cut, like a toll booth. A 92% leg is close to a sure thing, so it barely raises the price, only about 9%. But the toll for that leg can be 5 to 12%. If the toll is bigger than the bump, the payout goes down, and you're also carrying more risk. Second reason: legs that move together get priced as a pack. Embiid boards with Sixers ML, or Heat ML with Bam boards: if one hits the other usually does, so Kalshi gives you almost nothing for the second one.

                                                    The 10% bump test
                                                    use it

                                                    When you add a leg, watch the payout. If it doesn't jump at least 10% (a 3.00x needs to reach 3.30x), delete the leg. If it goes down, delete it twice as fast.

                                                    For a 70% leg the bump should be 40%+
                                                    The math, one line
                                                    keep it

                                                    Only add a leg if the new payout × our hit % for that leg beats the old payout. A 90% leg needs the payout up 11%. An 80% leg needs it up 25%.

                                                    If not, the leg is losing you money

                                                    Leg checker

                                                    New payout
                                                    Bump

                                                    Model v3 · the new rules, starting today

                                                    1. Coin flips stay in the lotto. Any leg under 60 never goes on the hammer, the 2x or the 5-10x.
                                                    2. Two-ticket max. One leg can ride on 2 tickets, not 5. Spread the risk.
                                                    3. New-team cap. Traded stars max out at 75 for their first 10 games on the new team.
                                                    4. 10% bump test. Every leg has to move the payout at least 10% or it comes off.
                                                    5. Plan, then stop. 4 tickets a day: hammer, 2x, 5-10x, one lotto. A late add has to replace a ticket, not stack on top.
                                                    6. Budget split. Hammer 35%, 2x 30%, 5-10x 25%, lottos 10%. On a 4.0 🍪 day: 1.4 🍪 / 1.2 🍪 / 1.0 🍪 / 0.4 🍪.

                                                        How we grade now updated Nov 20 · Engine v8

                                                        Loading the current record.

                                                        • Engine v8 (from the Nov 20 late games)Four AI analysts grade every leg blind: no Kalshi or sportsbook price is shown, so they have to do the research (minutes and role, injuries and news, the matchup and primary defender, shot zones, rest and travel, pace, and weather for football). Our grade is the middle of their four numbers plus our own system grade. Then Kalshi referees: at or above us is GREEN, 1 to 7 below us is YELLOW, and 8 or more below us is pulled, because that gap has lost most often in our record. Each agent also runs 1,000 simulations per game on near-even lines, shown on Research, Beta Test Mode.FROM NOV 20
                                                        • Engine v7 (Nov 20 early games)Four AI models grade every leg, starting from the Kalshi price and moving off it only for a named reason. We publish the middle of their numbers, capped at Kalshi + 7. If that middle number is 8 or more above Kalshi, the leg is removed from the board, the Hammer and every ticket, and shown on Research as "market disagrees". Legs with no Kalshi price max out at 75 and never go on the Hammer. The board shows GREEN legs (Kalshi at or above us) and YELLOW legs (1 to 7 above) graded 70+. Our own system grade is still computed and saved next to the models' numbers.FROM NOV 20
                                                        • Hammer under v73 to 5 legs from different games, each published 75+ with Kalshi at or above us or within 3, points, assists, threes or favorite moneylines, no back-to-backs, paying 2x or more. If fewer than 3 legs qualify, there is no Hammer that night. Passing is a win.FROM NOV 20
                                                        • EV Hammer2 to 5 legs from different games that Kalshi prices 80 to 92 cents and our grade agrees with (not 8+ above Kalshi, models within 12 points). The ticket posts only if it pays 1.5x or more after fees and our math expects at least +2% per dollar. If none qualifies, the best +2% ticket paying 1.35x or more at a 60%+ chance posts as the Safe Hammer. Otherwise we pass. Tracked as equal $1 bets from Nov 21; it switches itself off if it loses over 60+ legs.FROM NOV 21 · REPLACES THE 2X RULE
                                                        • Through Nov 19, grades came from our original processEach pick is graded from the player's season hit rate on that line, his last 5 games, the matchup and back-to-backs, then capped. Team lines are graded from the sportsbook spread. The Kalshi price is shown next to every leg but never changes the grade.CURRENT
                                                        • ⚠ legs stay off Hammers and main ticketsA ⚠ means our grade is 8 or more points above Kalshi. Those legs hit less often than the rest on the Nov 4 to 17 record, including nights that were not used to set the rule. On the 184 like-for-like picks from Nov 16 to 18 (Kalshi price taken when we graded), ⚠ legs hit 18 of 37 (49%), against 38 of 58 (66%) when we were 0 to 7 above Kalshi and 63 of 89 (71%) when we were below it. Those 37 legs came from 20 games, so this is still a small sample. Nov 19 added 30 more like-for-like legs: ⚠ legs hit 2 of 8, 0 to 7 above Kalshi 0 of 4, below Kalshi 7 of 18. Kalshi's prices were closer to the results than our grades again (accuracy score 0.279 vs 0.313, lower is better).SET NOV 18 · UPDATED NOV 19
                                                        • Old Hammer rule: every leg 80+ with Kalshi within 767-7 on Nov 4 to 17, against 23-22 for 80+ legs outside it. The rule was picked after seeing that data. Replaced by the v7 Hammer from Nov 20.RETIRED NOV 20
                                                        • Beta Test Mode is experimental1,000 simulated games per game on Kalshi lines near even money. It has one night of results and read high on that night (72% simulated, 60% actual).TESTING
                                                        • No category is called an edge yetOn 184 like-for-like picks (Nov 16 to 18: same picks, Kalshi price taken when we graded, grades that did not use Kalshi), Kalshi was more accurate than our grades (Brier 0.210 vs 0.224, lower is better; three nights, so provisional), and our 85+ grades hit about 72%. Many legs share a game or a player, so the real sample is smaller than the leg count.CURRENT

                                                        Everything below this panel is our first study, from Nov 4 to 7 (211 legs). It is kept as written for the record. Some of its findings did not hold up on later nights. For current numbers use Record and Research.

                                                        How easy is three? the model, explained for a 10-year-old

                                                        Picture a jar of 100 marbles. 78 are green, 22 are red. That's our 70%+ legs: 68 of 83 hit since Nov 4. A parlay is reaching in and pulling marbles. You only cash if every marble is green.

                                                        Tap the button to pull three marbles from the jar at random.

                                                        Hitting is not the same as profit
                                                        price matters

                                                        Three green marbles happens about 47 times in 100. But Kalshi prices a 3-leg like that around 1.6x to 1.8x, so you win about $0.70 when it hits and lose $1 when it misses. Over time that loses about 15 to 25 cents per dollar: a ticket that hits 47% of the time needs about 2.1x just to break even. The edge comes from legs the market prices worse than we grade them, and from passing on bad prices.

                                                        Grades are our estimates, not promises. 21+, bet what you can lose.
                                                        How we use the jar now
                                                        current rules

                                                        From Nov 21: legs where we grade 8 or more above Kalshi are pulled. A ticket posts only when its legs (Kalshi 80 to 92 cents, graded 75+) pay 1.5x or more after fees and our math expects at least +2% per dollar, or 1.35x+ at a 60%+ chance as the Safe Hammer. Otherwise we pass. Older rules on this page are kept as history.

                                                        Grades are our estimates, not promises. 21+, bet what you can lose.

                                                            "The hammers are great, let's keep winning. But let's also find a way to win a lotto, even if it's 20 70%s."Ace, Nov 8

                                                            Was the 17 of 20 just variance?

                                                            Partly. The three misses on Nov 6 were Luka over 6.5 assists (5), Castle 4+ rebounds (3) and Naz Reid 15+ (14). Naz was a true hook. Luka and Castle were categories we now flag: assist overs and guard rebound overs. Two of three were the ticket, not luck.

                                                            The clean 70 pool

                                                            Every 70%+ leg from Nov 4 to 8, NBA and NFL only: 44 of 50 hit (88%). All six misses sit in a flagged category: Huerter and Castle guard rebounds, Fagnano backup QB, Harden and McCollum on new teams, Avdija on a back-to-back. Take those out and every day's pool went perfect.

                                                            Honest read: those filters were written after we saw the misses, so 100% is the best case, not the forecast. Plan around 88 to 90% per leg until the next two weeks confirm it.

                                                            What a 70%-only lotto hits

                                                            Each bar is the chance every leg hits, at 88% per leg (white tick: 85%). A 20-leg of clean 70s is about 1 in 13. A 12-leg is about 1 in 5.

                                                            The algorithm · run this on every capper board

                                                            1. Pool. Only legs I grade 70%+. NBA and NFL. No college football, no UFC.
                                                            2. Filter. Cut any leg that hits a flag: backup or new QB on passing and receiving legs, guard rebound overs, assist overs, PRA combos, back-to-backs, players new to a team, James Harden.
                                                            3. Hook check. If the line sits within one of the player's average, drop one rung.
                                                            4. Spread it out. Separate games. Two legs from one game only when they share a script, like a favorite's ML plus its lead back.
                                                            5. Build the ladder. Core 8 (about 1 in 3), Ladder 12 (about 1 in 5), and the 20 only on slates with 20 clean legs. Never pad with 60s to reach 20.
                                                            6. Spice, max two. One star ceiling line in a good script and one top TD pick. Each roughly doubles the payout. Top 4 TDs went 3 of 4 Sunday.
                                                            7. Shop the price. Kalshi paid 10 to 30% of fair on long combos. Price the 12 and the 20 somewhere else before locking.
                                                            8. Size it. 0.1 🍪 to 0.2 🍪 a lotto. The hammer stays the main bet.

                                                                Structure math your 2-leg vs 7-leg question

                                                                You're right that two 55% legs can beat seven 80% legs. What decides it is the edge on each leg: how often it hits compared with what the price assumes. Here are three ways to build the same 1.0 🍪 using our actual hit rates.

                                                                Every build works when each leg has real edge. The losing build is the one we kept making: big tickets padded with 60s-tier alt-downs, where each leg hits less often than its price assumes.
